reasons: No tests are visible for the page or its consent behaviour.
Height and weight are not checked for sensible ranges in this file.
The consent labels depend on exact purpose names, so a naming change on the server would break the display.
Medical data is sent in full on each save without a visible comparison of changes.

terms.meaning: India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act of 2023, a law about how personal data must be handled and when consent is needed.
A clear yes or no from the user that allows the app to use their data for a stated purpose.
The named reason for a consent, such as AI summarization or core data processing.
The data bundle sent to the server in one request.
Values the page remembers while it is open, such as what the user typed or whether editing is on.
A shared place in the app for values like the signed-in user, used across pages.

used_by: Linked from the Profile item in the dashboard layout

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for profile page
sections.what: Loads icons, buttons, form field and card parts, the message helper, the auth store and the server connection.
sections.why: These are the pieces the page needs to draw itself and save changes.

sections.name: ProfilePage (part 1)
sections.title: Profile state and initial load
sections.what: Holds the consent switches, the editing flag, and all form fields. On open, it asks for the user details and consent records together, fills the form with the user's values, and sets consent flags.
sections.why: Loading both together means the page is ready once, and the form starts with real data.
sections.watch_out: If the user request fails, the form stays empty with no visible reason beyond the error message.

sections.name: ProfilePage (part 2)
sections.title: Consent toggle and form change
sections.what: Turns a consent on or off by asking the server, then updates the local flag and shows a message. The form change handler copies each typed value into the matching field.
sections.why: Each consent change is recorded on the server so the change is kept between visits.
sections.watch_out: Consent is only changed locally after the server accepts the request, so the displayed state can lag briefly.

sections.name: ProfilePage (part 3)
sections.title: Saving profile changes
sections.what: Blocks saving when the full name is empty, converts height and weight to numbers, sends the changes, updates the signed-in name and email locally, and turns editing off.
sections.why: Checks the name before sending so the user gets a fast message, and updates the local user so headers match.
sections.watch_out: Empty height or weight becomes null on save, so clearing a field removes the stored value.

sections.name: ProfilePage: if
sections.title: Loading placeholder and page header
sections.what: Shows a pulsing placeholder while loading. Then draws the heading and the Edit Profile button, or Cancel and Save Profile while editing.
sections.why: Placeholders stop the page from looking broken while data loads.
sections.watch_out: Cancel only switches editing off, so typed changes stay in the form until the page is reloaded.

sections.name: ProfilePage (part 5)
sections.title: Personal details fields
sections.what: Draws the card with full name, email, phone, date of birth and gender. The email field is locked when the user already has an email on their account.
sections.why: Basic identity details are grouped together, and the email lock avoids accidental changes to the login email.
sections.watch_out: The email lock only checks the user record, so a user without an email can still edit it.

sections.name: ProfilePage (part 6)
sections.title: Medical indicators fields
sections.what: Draws blood group, height and weight. Blood group is a fixed list of choices, while height and weight are number fields with one decimal.
sections.why: Keeps common clinical values in standard, easy-to-read formats.
sections.watch_out: The blood group list is hard-coded, so adding a new group needs a code change.

sections.name: ProfilePage (part 7)
sections.title: Emergency contact field
sections.what: Draws one field for the emergency contact phone number.
sections.why: Lets the user record who to call in an emergency.
sections.watch_out: The field accepts any text, so a typing mistake is only caught by the server if it checks.

sections.name: ProfilePage (part 8)
sections.title: Consent card and AI consent
sections.what: Shows the consent card with a DPDP badge, then the AI summarization consent with a status tag and a grant or revoke button. The text explains that revoking stops AI processing.
sections.why: Gives the user a clear choice about AI processing of their medical records, which the law requires them to be able to change.
sections.watch_out: The explanation names a specific stop message, so any change in the server's wording needs this text updated too.

sections.name: ProfilePage (part 9)
sections.title: Core data consent and closing tags
sections.what: Shows the core health data consent with its status and button, then closes the form and page. The text says this consent is needed for the unified timeline.
sections.why: Lets the user control storage of their health history separately from AI use.
sections.watch_out: Revoking this consent may break the timeline, but the page does not warn about that before the change is made.

summary: The profile page where a signed-in user views and edits personal and medical details, emergency contact, and grants or withdraws consent for data use.
purpose: Lets the user keep their health details accurate and control two consent choices that the app needs for legal and clinical reasons.
why: Consent for AI processing and core data storage has to be recorded and changeable, so the page provides both controls in one place.
how: On load, the page fetches the user's details and their consent records at the same time. It fills the form and marks each consent as active or withdrawn. Editing is turned on by a button. Saving converts height and weight to numbers, sends the update to the server, updates the signed-in user's name and email locally, then turns editing off. Consent buttons send a grant or revoke request for each purpose.
inputs: The user's details from the server, typed values in the form, and clicks on Edit, Save, Cancel and consent buttons.
outputs: Updated profile data sent to the server, updated consent records, and success or error messages.
risks: Revoking AI consent stops AI processing, and the page says so. Core data consent revoke is also available here and may affect the timeline. Height and weight are converted with no range check, so odd values can be saved. The page relies on server checks for input.
debug: If the form is blank, check the user request in the browser network tab and the mapping in the load function. If saving fails, read the error in the console and check the update request. If consent shows the wrong state, check the consent list returned by the server and its purpose names. If the email field is locked, it is locked because the user already has an email on their account.
